_what_this_is: Every KNOWN_BAD golden fixture carries a `_must_fail_because` list. Until this
file existed, `scripts/contract-check.py::pass_fixtures` asked only whether the
fixture produced AT LEAST ONE schema error. An independent reviewer reduced
transfer_evidence.schema.json in memory to a single `bundle_kind` const:
the valid fixture still produced zero errors, the known-bad still produced one,
and the gate stayed GREEN while essentially every other C11 constraint had
disappeared. N promised reasons, one demonstrated failure, and any surviving
failure masking the loss of the others.
`_must_fail_because` is PROSE and prose cannot be checked. This file is the
machine-checkable half: for each declared reason, the exact place and keyword
that must fire. It is READ BY `pass_proven`, which requires:
P1  every KNOWN_BAD fixture on disk has an entry here
P2  the entry declares exactly as many reasons as the fixture does
P3  each `claim` is a literal substring of the reason it is bound to, so a
reason rewritten in the generator without touching this file goes RED
P4  every `evidence` triple matches at least one real validation error
P5  no two reasons in one fixture claim the IDENTICAL evidence triple; N
reasons must be N failures, not one failure counted N times
P6  every `external` code fires in the replay reader, and a code recorded
`not_reachable` must NOT fire (a stale escape is a finding)
P7  every validation error is claimed by some reason or recorded in
`unexplained_errors`, and a recorded one that stops firing is stale
P8  no entry here names a fixture that is not on disk
`unenforced` is the one escape and it is policed in BOTH directions. It records
a reason the schema does not actually enforce, names the constraint that would
enforce it, and carries `would_be`: the evidence triple the reason WOULD produce.
The gate asserts that triple does NOT match today. The moment someone adds the
constraint, this record goes stale and the gate goes RED, which is how the
record gets promoted to `evidence` rather than sitting here forever.
SEVEN REASONS ACROSS FOUR CONTRACTS ARE RECORDED `unenforced`. That is the
finding, not a footnote: those fixtures' prose promises a rejection the schema
does not perform, and a lane reading the fixture would believe it does.
This file lives under `proof/` rather than beside the fixtures because
`pass_fixtures` globs `contracts/golden/*.json` and treats every file it finds
as an instance needing a mapped schema.
Nothing here was read from a sealed object. It names field paths in
hand-authored fixtures and nothing else.

unenforced.why_now: The schema owner deliberately left `args` open. Ruling 21 is stated there in prose, so a PRE-STAMP ToolEvent validates cleanly and this fixture's first declared reason never fires.

unenforced.needs: nothing new. This reason and reason 1 are THE SAME FAILURE stated twice: the single `additionalProperties` error naming `result`. Reason 1 already claims it, so binding this one too would let one surviving error stand in for two promised reasons, which is the exact defect this file exists to close.
unenforced.why_now: The fixture declares five reasons and can demonstrate four. Either merge 1 and 4 in the generator, or give reason 1 a distinct constraint (making `result_digest` required would do it, and is a schema decision, not a fixture one).

unenforced.needs: nothing new in the schema. THIS FIXTURE'S OWN SECOND DEFECT DISABLES ITS FIRST. `tools.items.allOf[0]` requires `beneficiary_key` on a CAP_MOVES_MONEY tool only when the tool is NOT `fail_closed`, and this tool sets `fail_closed: true` for reason 1. The carve-out is correct and documented; the fixture puts both defects on the same tool, so the conditional never reaches its `then`. The repair is a SECOND tool in the fixture carrying CAP_MOVES_MONEY with no beneficiary_key and no fail_closed.
unenforced.why_now: The fixture is generated by `scripts/make-golden.py`, which is owned elsewhere.

Even if one did, the schema types `destination_args` as an array of arg-path strings and has no declaration of each ARG's own type, so 'this named arg is list-valued at call time' is not expressible in C3a as written.
unenforced.why_now: This reason describes a runtime property of the target's arguments, not a shape of the manifest. It belongs in the D3 manifest-completeness check, not in a schema fixture.

reasons.claim: blindness_check result FAIL must block the freeze

unenforced.needs: `blindness_check.result` is `{"enum": ["PASS", "FAIL"]}`, so FAIL is a legal recorded value and a FROZEN derived schema carrying a FAILED blindness check validates. Enforcing the claim means `const: "PASS"` on the frozen artifact, or an `if result == FAIL then` clause that makes the document invalid.
unenforced.why_now: The enum is arguably right for a pre-freeze document and wrong for a frozen one. That is a C3b design decision and the schema is owned elsewhere.

unenforced.needs: `max_predictive_accuracy` is `{"type": "number"}` with no bound, so 1.0 validates. Ruling 19.3 says a field that perfectly predicts the label is a leak and is REMOVED; enforcing that here means `exclusiveMaximum` on the frozen document.
unenforced.why_now: Same as reason 2: it is a C3b design decision. This is the one the fixture's own text calls the leak that 'looks exactly like success', and today the schema cannot see it.

reasons.claim: capability_classes is a LIST on a RULE

unenforced.needs: THE FIXTURE CONTAINS NO RETRACT. Its single rule is `verb: deny` with `origin: seed`, which is a legal seed rule. Demonstrating the claim needs a rule with `verb: retract` targeting a seed-origin rule, and a schema clause forbidding it.
unenforced.why_now: The fixture is generated elsewhere, and the retract-vs-seed rule may be a validator invariant rather than a schema one. Either way this reason is decoration today: a lane repairing every other listed defect would see this fixture pass while believing the retract rule was tested.

unenforced.needs: THE FIXTURE CONTAINS NO reason_code AT ALL. Nothing in the document carries the field the reason describes.
unenforced.why_now: Same as reason 4. The claim is about the DSL's reason_code symbol table; the fixture never instantiates it.

This fixture fails for a THIRD reason its own `_must_fail_because` does not name: an INVALID verdict must carry `invalid_reason`, and this one does not. A lane repairing both listed reasons still sees red with nothing to tell it why. The fixture is generated by `scripts/make-golden.py`, owned elsewhere; the repair is one more line in its `_must_fail_because` list, not a schema change.
